title: Physiological markers of visual environment comfort in the North
research_question: To identify physiological markers of visual environment comfort of modern cities located in the polar and pre-polar regions of Russia.

participants.description: 50 people aged 20 years without any visual and nervous systems pathology, from modern cities located in the polar and pre-polar regions of Russia.

stimuli_or_exposures.description:
Five series of urban visual environment images, each presented for 30 seconds:
1.  **Series I (Historic buildings)**: Constructions from 18-19 centuries, low-rise, Baroque/classical/Gothic style, with carved details, varied colors, natural lines.
2.  **Series II (Modern buildings)**: Constructions from the last decade of the 21st century, high-tech/deconstructivism/postmodernism styles, monochrome slabs, mirror panels, minimalism, unusual forms.
3.  **Series III (Homogeneous)**: Gable facades without windows or other elements (standard of uncomfortable visual environment).
4.  **Series IV (Aggressive)**: Standardized multi-storey buildings with many identical windows (standard of uncomfortable visual environment).
5.  **Series V (Comfortable)**: Images of nature (standard of comfortable visual environment).

measures.construct: Autonomic Nervous System (ANS) response (Caused Skin Vegetative Potential - CSVP)

mechanisms: Activation of the ergotropic brain system providing body mobilization, corresponding to a stress response.
Delay in nerve center activation at the hypothalamus level activates trophotropic centers, increases parasympathetic tone, and provides an optimal mode of visual perception.
The eye scans the visible field in search of details, but since they are not available (in homogeneous environments), there is an increase in saccade number and amplitude.
Duration of fixations in homogeneous visual fields is used for new saccade programming, as saccadic automation is disturbed.
Visual information is either missing or identical in uncomfortable environments, requiring no thinking.
Intensive scanning of the visual field with short low-amplitude saccades and a small number of fixations causes overstrain of the visual system, fast fatigue, and psychological discomfort.
A stable interrelation is formed between visual field scanning processes and mental processing of visual information received by the brain in comfortable environments.
The variety of details in comfortable visual urban fields allows almost every saccade to end with a fixation.
An effective functional system, combining visual structures and ANS, is formed during perception of natural visual environments, providing an optimal mode of visual perception.
implementation_implications: To redress uncomfortable visual space, it is recommended to use wall painting, increase the number of park areas with art installations, and use a variety of color palettes when finishing with siding or painting building facades.
